candidates.title: Optimal-transport flow matching for stochastic model ipdating
candidates.abstract: Deep generative models have attracted considerable attention as inference engines for stochastic model updating. Among these deep generative models, conditional flow matching offers a particularly efficient formulation, in which a continuous transport map from a latent distribution to the posterior is learned by regression against optimal-transport probability paths, avoiding both the invertibility constraints of normalising flows and the iterative denoising of diffusion models. However, its performance in engineering model updating has not been examined against an established baseline such as the Bayesian updating framework under controlled conditions. In this work, conditional flow matching is therefore assessed against the Bayesian model updating approach with transitional Markov chain Monte Carlo, in which the Bhattacharyya distance provides the approximate likelihood for the Bayesian approach. The two methods are assessed with respect to posterior fidelity, evaluated by statistical distances against the known ground truth and computational expenditure in model evaluations, with the offline training budget reported separately from the inference cost of each subsequent conditioning. A 3-DOF spring–mass system with uncertain stiffness parameters serves as the benchmark. Since the calibrated posterior constitutes the input description upon which subsequent reliability assessment depends, the accuracy and the marginal cost of the updating step both bear directly on reliability computations. In addition, the amortised nature of the learned transport map is discussed in this work, as it permits the posterior to be re-evaluated under new observations at negligible cost, which is a property of practical relevance to reliability assessment under sequentially acquired monitoring data.

candidates.title: Research progress on the application of multi-scale computational methods in the research and development of anti-tuberculosis infection drugs
candidates.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), driven by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), remains a leading cause of mortality from infectious disease worldwide.​ The global dissemination of multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) strains—coupled with protracted treatment regimens and the persistence of latent infection—has not only compromised first-line chemotherapies but also underscored the stagnation of conventional drug development pipelines. In this review, we systematically synthesize how multi-scale computational strategies are reshaping anti-TB drug discovery and explicitly delineate their hierarchical integration—a cohesive framework that, to our knowledge, has yet to be comprehensively mapped in the existing literature.​ We survey four interconnected computational layers: (i) systems and network pharmacology for macroscopic target and pathway prioritization; (ii) machine learning (ML) for mesoscopic virtual screening, resistance classification, and ADMET prediction; (iii) molecular docking for microscopic elucidation of ligand–target binding modes; and (iv) molecular dynamics (MD) simulations for atomic-level validation of binding poses and assessment of complex stability. Representative studies demonstrate that this workflow has pinpointed pivotal TB vulnerabilities (e.g., MmpL3, InhA, DprE1, ATP synthase, and FtsZ), enabled ML models to predict drug resistance from genomic data with high fidelity, and identified promising candidates such as vazabitide A (predicted binding affinity of −85.8 kcal/mol against Pks13) alongside repurposed agents (e.g., aldoxorubicin, quarfloxin). Critically, these computational predictions are reinforced by orthogonal experimental validation spanning in vitro enzymatic and phenotypic assays, in vivo infection models, clinical pharmacokinetic profiling, and multi-omics corroboration. We conclude that the top-down pipeline-spanning network pharmacology to ML, docking, and MD-integrated with bottom-up feedback constitutes a closed-loop paradigm that accelerates lead identification while addressing emergent drug resistance.​ Nevertheless, inherent limitations in predictive reliability and cross-layer error propagation necessitate rigorous downstream experimental validation. Looking forward, generative artificial intelligence, self-driving laboratories, and standardized cross-method benchmarking are poised to consolidate this multi-scale pipeline into a robust engine for next-generation anti-TB therapeutics.

candidates.title: Subpocket-Aware Fragment-Based Docking Pipeline for Kinase Ligand Design: Methodology and a PKA Case Study
candidates.abstract: Abstract Protein kinases regulate signal transduction through phosphorylation, and their dysregulation drives diseases like cancer, autoimmune disorders, and Alzheimer’s, making them key drug targets. Fragment-based drug design offers a powerful route to kinase inhibitors but often neglects kinase-specific structural insights. While KinFragLib, a library consisting of 7486 fragments derived from kinase-ligand complexes, provides a rich resource, exhaustive recombination of its fragments is computationally demanding. Here, we present an efficient exploration strategy that integrates subpocket-guided fragment growing with template docking to navigate this vast chemical space. Our automated pipeline prioritizes kinase-specific structural information, enabling targeted generation of chemically diverse ligands. Applied to the PKA kinase, the approach produced 33758 candidate molecules with promising docking scores, of which 15 were synthesized. Seven molecules reduced kinase activity by more than 50% at an inhibitor concentration of 100 μM, and five of these compounds also showed promising efficacy at a concentration of 10 μM. The IC50 determination ultimately revealed that five of the molecules were effective in the two- to three-digit nanomolar range. Crystallographic validation confirmed the predicted binding mode of the most potent compound. This methodology demonstrates how structure-informed guidance can transform fragment-based design into a scalable route for discovering novel kinase inhibitors.

candidates.title: Beyond SELEX: AI-driven aptamers from sequence to structure to function.
candidates.abstract: Conventional aptamer discovery by systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment (SELEX) is often constrained by limited library capacity, PCR bias, and multi-round screening. The recent convergence of artificial intelligence with aptamer development is driving a paradigm shift from empirical screening toward rational, data-driven design. This Review presents a timely and comprehensive overview of AI integration across the entire aptamer development pipeline, with a particular emphasis on advances reported in 2024-2026. We begin by discussing bioinformatics databases and computational tools for high-throughput SELEX data analysis. We then review state-of-the-art strategies for secondary and tertiary structure prediction, including recent breakthroughs such as AlphaFold 3, RoseTTAFoldNA, and diffusion-based approaches. We also cover machine learning methods for aptamer-target interaction prediction, molecular docking, dynamics simulations, and free energy calculations. A major focus is placed on very recent AI-driven generative design, including diffusion models (AptaDiff), language model-based frameworks (InstructNA, GRAPE-LM), and reinforcement learning approaches (AiDTA) for de novo aptamer generation and optimization. Emerging applications of AI-designed aptamers in precision diagnostics, targeted therapy, and biosensing are also surveyed. Finally, we discuss current challenges and outline future directions toward closed-loop, interpretable AI frameworks for translational aptamer development. By synthesizing the latest computational and experimental advances, this Review aims to serve as a timely resource for researchers seeking to leverage AI for next-generation aptamer discovery.

candidates.title: OmniVerifier-C1: Decomposed Graded Verifier for Rule-Governed Generative World Modeling
candidates.abstract: Generative visual verifiers play a crucial role in advancing multimodal intelligence. To enhance the robustness of visual verifiers in complex multimodal scenarios involving compositional requirements, we move beyond conventional binary verifiers that produce only True/False discrete judgments and introduce a verifier that automatically decomposes complex prompts or environmental rules into fine-grained components and assigns pointwise scores to provide a continuous and more informative critique signal. Our experiments further demonstrate that these structured and interpretable outputs improve the verifier's generalization to out-of-domain multimodal critic tasks. To train this verifier, we introduce a Decoupled RL training strategy that jointly optimizes sub-question-level binary judgment and global alignment scoring, using precise local feedback to develop fine-grained verification capabilities that provide a foundation for reliable continuous scoring at the global level. Under a general reinforcement learning framework, we first empirically demonstrate that the proposed pointwise graded verifier significantly outperforms binary verifiers in traditional text-to-image scenarios. We then extend our investigation to rule-governed generative world modeling where generative models are leveraged for world simulation and world reasoning under explicit rules. From a theoretical standpoint, we further show that a pairwise verification paradigm yields more accurate critiques than the pointwise formulation when ground-truth images are available, with empirical results on diverse structured world-modeling tasks such as Maze and Sudoku further validating the effectiveness of our approach. Overall, our findings suggest a key insight: the transition from generative models to structured world-modeling agents critically hinges on the availability of accurate pairwise graded visual verifiers.

candidates.title: Converting FGFR inhibitors into selective covalent molecular glue degraders via transposable gluing handles.
candidates.abstract: Molecular glue degraders (MGDs) have emerged as a transformative therapeutic modality, offering the potential to deplete undruggable or pathogenic proteins. However, the rational design of MGDs remains inherently challenging compared to traditional heterobifunctional degraders. Recently, the implementation of transposable chemical gluing handles has provided an efficient approach to convert established protein-targeting ligands into target-specific MGDs. In this study, by incorporating diverse molecular glue handles and amino acid-based degrons into the solvent-exposed exit vectors of infigratinib, we synthesized a library of 30 candidate MGDs. Preliminary screening and subsequent lead optimization identified LC-MG-5 and LC-MG-10 as highly efficient degraders of FGFR2. In cellular models, both compounds demonstrated potent suppression of FGFR2-mediated signaling pathways. Mechanistic investigations revealed that the covalent engagement of the gluing handle is a critical determinant for successful proteasomal degradation of FGFR2. This work provides a framework for the rational transformation of kinase inhibitors into covalent molecular glue degraders, underscoring the potential of FGFR degradation as a next-generation precision medicine strategy for FGFR2-driven malignancies.

candidates.title: Poisoning the corpora of protein design systems during pre-training and retrieval
candidates.abstract: Protein foundation models increasingly support the generation of novel biological sequences, yet their reliance on large public datasets creates opportunities for adversarial manipulation of the material they learn from and retrieve. We investigate two data-only poisoning attacks against protein design systems, targeting the pre-training corpus of autoregressive protein language models and the retrieval corpus of a text-guided protein generator. For the first, we pre-trained ProtGPT2 and ProGen2 variants of 300 million parameters, introducing poisoned protein sequences containing one of two triggers followed by one of three payloads. Across all poisoned runs, both architectures acquired highly reliable trigger-dependent generation under uniform and ramped poisoning schedules. Under ramped exposure, the earliest majority activation occurred after only 200 contaminated examples, while for the uniform schedule earliest activation occurred around 5000 poisoned samples. For the second attack, we inserted records into a retrieval corpus system without modifying its weights or decoding procedure. A single query-aware record captured a top-16 retrieval position for 58\% of templated requests and 97\% of free-text requests. Conditional on successful poisoned retrieval, 62\% of requests produced altered sequences, while 19-21% acquired the inserted domain by profile-HMM homology. A universal query-unaware attack using 1,500 records also achieved substantial retrieval capture and domain transfer. Together, these findings demonstrate that adversarial protein sequence contributions can establish persistent, sequence-specific behaviour during pre-training or redirect protein generation at inference, while leaving ordinary model behaviour largely preserved. Our work establishes the integrity and biological provenance of protein sequence data as critical safeguards for generative protein design systems.

candidates.title: Virus-like particle vaccines: from antigen architecture to antigen presentation and adaptive immune responses
candidates.abstract: Introduction Virus-like particles (VLPs) mimic key structural features of native viruses while lacking a replication-competent viral genome, combining favorable safety with multivalent antigen presentation and strong immunogenicity. Yet, how VLP design influences the quality and persistence of adaptive immunity remains incompletely understood.Areas covered This review examines relevant literature identified through targeted searches on recent advances in VLP engineering, with emphasis on particle architecture, antigen-display strategies, and structural determinants of immune recognition. We discuss how VLPs facilitate antigen presentation by antigen-presenting cells and shape CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell responses, immune memory, and T follicular helper cell–B-cell interactions within germinal centers. Emerging approaches linking VLP design with humoral and cellular immunity are also considered.Expert opinion The next generation of VLP vaccines will require a transition from empirical enhancement of immunogenicity toward precision engineering of immune responses. A major challenge is to establish robust and transferable structure–immunity relationships while addressing manufacturing feasibility, quality control, potency assessment, and product comparability. Advances in computational protein design, structural biology, and high-dimensional immune profiling are expected to enable increasingly quantitative and mechanism-based optimization of VLP platforms. However, fully predictive control over human immune responses will remain a complex challenge.

candidates.title: Evaluation of Physics-Based Pose Prediction and the Role of Receptor Flexibility in a Community Antiviral Blind Challenge
candidates.abstract: Abstract Prediction of protein–ligand binding modes is a key step in computer-aided drug design, since incorrect pose prediction inevitably limits the achievable accuracy of downstream physics-based affinity predictions. The ASAP-Polaris-OpenADMET antiviral competition was launched in 2025 as a means to prospectively test computational methods across a range of measurements that guide early prioritization during a drug discovery campaign including pose prediction. Here, we describe our two open-source, physics-based entries to the pose prediction challenge, which are based on templated molecular growth with hybrid machine learning/molecular mechanics interatomic potentials. We show that our approach was among the top-performing physics-based methods, and with a retrospective change to the workflow to make greater use of the training data as templates, we obtain a success rate of 74% across SARS-CoV-2 and MERS-CoV main protease target protein structures. Finally, we investigate the importance of receptor side-chain flexibility on retrospective performance. We find that building poses against an ensemble of feasible side-chain conformers is useful in generating improved binding poses but that the tested scoring functions are unable to successfully pick out native structures from the generated ensemble.

candidates.title: Query-Efficient Rejection Sampling for Parallel Masked Diffusion
candidates.abstract: Masked diffusion models (MDMs) accelerate generation by unmasking multiple tokens in parallel, but sampling these tokens independently ignores their correlations and biases the output. Anari et al. (2026) corrected this bias with rejection sampling, decomposing the log acceptance probability into a sum of token-level terms, but the evaluation requires one score query per unmasked token. We propose the Single-Increment Rejection Sampler (SIRS), which provides an estimate of the log acceptance probability from a single randomly sampled increment at the cost of one query. SIRS then converts a Poisson number of clipped estimates into accept/reject decisions through a Bernoulli factory adapted from Chen et al. (2026). Since each query returns the conditionals of all remaining tokens in the block, we further Rao-Blackwellize each increment by averaging over these tokens at no extra cost, thereby reducing clipping. We show that the KL-divergence between the data distribution and the SIRS output is bounded by a clipping term plus the model's training error. With exact scores, parallel decoding pays the full within-block dependence, whereas SIRS pays only the part beyond the clipping range.

candidates.title: Integrating Remote Sensing, Multi-Objective Optimization, and Agent-Based Modelling for Nature-Based Flood Mitigation
candidates.abstract: By 2030, pluvial flooding is estimated to cause nearly $500 billion in global damage, affecting 54 million people (UNDRR, 2015) each year. By 2050, metropolitan assets worth around $158 trillion could be at risk of floods. This rising risk has sparked an increased interest in nature-based solutions (NbS), as traditional hydraulic infrastructure may lack the flexibility required to manage more complex flood hazards. This study looks into the use of a data-driven approach to identify and assess the effectiveness of upstream afforestation in preventing pluvial floods. We constructed a thorough computational framework for the Girona/Empordà region of Catalonia, Spain. This framework combines cloud-based remote sensing via Google Earth Engine, multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA), multi-objective evolutionary optimisation via NSGA-II, and agent-based flood simulation, which is linked to a reinforcement learning agent based on Proximal Policy Optimisation. The framework functions on two stacked spatial scales. At a regional scale (20 x 20 km), it finds and selects suitable afforestation patches. At a meso scale (1 x 1 km), it simulates flood responses to various afforestation schemes. The findings illustrate the technological viability of combining different methods into a single computing process. Preliminary reinforcement-learning results indicate a directional improvement in simulated flood outcomes.

candidates.title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
candidates.abstract: Time series foundation models are becoming increasingly popular for general-purpose forecasting. However, most leading models predict marginal quantiles, leaving the dependence structure of future trajectories unspecified. This distinction matters for trajectory-dependent quantities such as cumulative demand, peak load, and event timing, yet point and marginal scores do not reveal it. To model this dependence, we introduce PathFM, a trajectory-based forecasting model that uses flow matching to generate complete future paths. We further distill the model to one or two steps and share history attention cache across draws. Together, these enable PathFM to generate multiple paths for a single series in roughly the time needed for one query to a quantile model. The distilled sampler also makes it practical to optimize a calibration loss directly. PathFM achieves competitive marginal accuracy on the established forecasting benchmarks fev-bench and TIME. To complement these evaluations, we introduce Forecast Path Score Bench (fps-bench), which augments fev-bench tasks with energy and variogram scores and downstream metrics. PathFM achieves a higher aggregate path score on fps-bench than all evaluated external baselines. Experiments on chaotic systems further show that our flow model sustains long-run variability, while strong baselines rapidly collapse. PathFM makes generative time series forecasting both competitive and practical, enabling diverse downstream applications.

candidates.title: Spatial Statistics for Screening Molecular Structures
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT The dominant paradigm in computational materials discovery relies on heavily parameterized deep architectures, including message‐passing graph and equivariant networks, that typically require large density functional theory (DFT)‐labeled training sets and produce nonconvex latent representations complicating inverse design, a limitation in the data‐scarce regimes common to exploratory screening. Standard formulations also face specific difficulties with chemically disordered configurations and with distinguishing chiral geometries (e.g., ‐invariant models are reflection‐blind by construction). These are task‐ and formulation‐dependent tendencies, not universal deficiencies, and are reduced by pre‐training, transfer, and equivariant designs. This review presents spatial‐statistics feature engineering as a physically rigorous, deployable complement. Molecular structures are encoded as voxelized fields, and two‐point auto‐ and cross‐correlations are evaluated deterministically via Fast Fourier Transforms, moving spatial pattern recognition into a closed‐form, physics‐informed operation. Principal component analysis yields low‐dimensional, convex representations supporting lean neural networks and non‐parametric surrogates, achieving sub‐2% normalized errors from as little as 0.1% of the dataset in reported cases. Demonstrated across periodic crystals, disordered high‐entropy alloys, and non‐periodic molecules, the framework enables Bayesian active learning and zero‐shot extrapolation on commodity hardware, which remains challenging for large‐scale architectures at equal data budgets.

candidates.title: scMTG reconstructs single-cell temporal dynamics with Markov transition generators
candidates.abstract: Single-cell time-series data offer a unique opportunity to study how cell states emerge, evolve, and diversify over time. However, cells are destructively measured across time points and individual cells cannot be directly tracked, making it challenging to reconstruct cell-state transitions and uncover the dynamic regulatory programs. Existing methods are predominantly based on optimal transport and typically require predefined low-dimensional representations, which can limit scalability, flexibility, and mechanistic interpretability. Here we present scMTG, a single-cell Markov transition generative framework that jointly learns cell representations and temporal cell-state transitions from unpaired single-cell time-series data. In a series of experiments, scMTG demonstrates superior performance in interpolating held-out missing-time-point data and inferring cross-time-point transition matrices, compared with state-of-the-art methods. More importantly, the learned Markov transition generator provides an interpretable framework for identifying the molecular programs that drive cell-state changes, enabling characterization of cell fate decisions and construction of time-resolved regulatory networks. Together, scMTG provides a unified generative framework for reconstructing cellular dynamics and uncovering regulatory programs that shape development, differentiation, and disease progression. scMTG is available as open-source software at https://github.com/liuq-lab/scMTG.

candidates.title: Rethinking Successive Rejects Algorithms
candidates.abstract: In the best-arm identification problem, an algorithm adaptively selects arms to find the arm of the largest mean reward. Successive Rejects (SR) is a simple fixed-budget best-arm identification algorithm that eliminates one candidate arm at each phase. At first glance, SR seems to have limited adaptivity, since it follows predetermined phase lengths. However, for Gaussian arms with common variance, SR's worst-instance error exponent normalized by the popular complexity measure $H_1(P)$ is optimal up to a constant factor, which partly explains why SR's performance is competitive compared with state-of-the-art adaptive sampling algorithms. In this paper, we extend the framework of SR by optimizing its predefined schedule of phase lengths. We formulate phase-schedule design as an optimization problem for the normalized error exponent. Then, we introduce a version of SR with the optimized schedule, which we call $H_1$-balanced Successive Rejects ($H_1$-SR). This schedule is optimal within the class of SR-type algorithms with deterministic equal-count schedules. For Gaussian arms with common variance, $H_1$-SR achieves at least $11/12$ of the optimal normalized rate over all adaptive algorithms for every $K\ge2$, and this approximation ratio converges to one as $1-O(1/\log K)$ as $K\to\infty$. This is a significant improvement over original SR, whose corresponding fraction of the optimal normalized rate converges to $1/4$. Finally, experiments on ten synthetic instances and two dataset-derived Gaussian benchmarks compare the optimized schedule with original SR at finite horizons. They show substantial gains on many instances while also exposing a regime in which more aggressive early elimination is costly.

candidates.title: Predicting Unseen Scientific Interactions: Conditional Flow Models Hallucinate Non-Additive Effects
candidates.abstract: Conditional generative models are increasingly used for scientific prediction beyond the direct training support. Yet scientific questions often concern whether one intervention changes the effect of another. Such interactions can be of primary interest while explaining little of the total variation, allowing models to appear accurate overall without recovering the relevant scientific effect. It remains unclear how these models learn interactions and when these successfully extrapolate to unseen conditions. We therefore study interaction recovery in flow-matching models using a physiological time-series simulator, drug dose-response data, combinatorial cell perturbations, and molecular conformer generations, where we separate recovery from hallucinated interaction structure. In the controlled setting, individual effects are learned much earlier than interactions and models hallucinate interactions where none exist. Across settings, we find qualitatively different generalization problems, with successful prediction depending on whether condition structure continues from observed to held-out targets. When it does, interactions are recoverable. If not, models can generate plausible responses while missing the interaction. We furthermore find that hallucinations increase as targets become less identifiable, and that successful interaction recovery in output space can fail under nonlinear readouts. Finally, we show that aggregate fidelity metrics can conceal whether models learn and extrapolate interactions.

candidates.title: Investigation and Optimization of Air Pollution Risk by a Multi-criteria Decision Making Method Using Fuzzy TOPSIS: A Case Study of Construction Workers
candidates.abstract: Background: Investigating human health during work importantly affect the safety and efficiency of the society. Different types of activity, including industrial, constructional, heavy duty ones, etc., affect the health of workers during their activities. In this study, the Multi-Objective Decision-Making (MODM) method was combined with fuzzy TOPSIS to investigate and optimize the air pollution risk affecting the health and safety of construction workers of Lar City, Fars Province, Iran. Methods: The comparison matrices (binary) and the Phillips–Perron test of different criteria and sub-criteria of health risk, including safety view, safety efficiency, understanding the risk, and risk investigation, were assessed to find the most influential factors for the optimization of the health risk of the workers. Results: Accordingly, the results indicated that “understanding the risk” followed by “safety efficiency” affected the health risk of the construction workers the most. However, among the sub-criteria, the most effective ones were “worker knowledge”, “manager knowledge”, “logistic specialized managers”, “modern facilities”, and “modern technology”. The selection of the linear and non-linear models was conducted according to the F values, and the model parameters were estimated using the Newton-Raphson test. Most coefficients were significant at P= 0.99. The model also has a high describing value of 0.97. The final estimated homogeneity coefficient was equal to 1.31, and it ranged from 0.86 to 2.72 for the critical risk investigation. The significance of the present research is to increase the health and safety of workers during work resulting in a more sustainable and healthier environment. Conclusion: Accordingly, the managers could handle the risks, determine the tolerable risks, indicate the risk of each process to control expenses, and take the essential measures for optimization.

candidates.title: Learning Dynamic Protein Representations at Scale with Distograms
candidates.abstract: Protein function and other biological properties often depend on structural dynamics, yet most machine-learning predictors rely on static representations. Physics-based molecular simulations can describe conformational variability but remain computationally prohibitive at scale. Generative models provide a more efficient alternative, though their ability to produce accurate conformational ensembles is still limited. In this work, we bypass expensive simulations by leveraging residue-residue distance probability distributions (distograms) from structure predictors such as Boltz-2. Our approach provides a scalable way to encode dynamic information into protein representations, aiming to improve function prediction without explicit conformational sampling. All code required to reproduce the experiments presented in this work is publicly available at https://github.com/anonymous-research-world/distodyn.

candidates.title: Lean Graph Search for Formal Theorem Proving
candidates.abstract: Retrieving relevant lemmas is crucial for formal theorem proving, enabling provers to build machine-checkable proofs from established mathematical results. Recent retrieval systems match library declarations to a target theorem or its intermediate proof steps, but make limited use of multi-hop dependencies among declarations. These dependencies can reveal supporting lemmas that are not necessarily lexically similar to the target theorem but recur in proofs of related problems. To this end, we propose LeanGraphSearch, a graph-based retrieval method for Lean 4 that constructs a graph from Mathlib's forward dependencies and traverses it to uncover supporting lemmas through multi-hop dependency chains. Specifically, LeanGraphSearch links each declaration to the premises it depends on, uses a graph-based ranking algorithm to propagate relevance from semantically matched declarations to their dependencies, and reranks the expanded candidates against the original query. Across two mathematical retrieval benchmarks, LeanGraphSearch improves recall by up to 12% over the strongest baseline, LeanSearch v2, on MathlibQR and increases coverage of complete annotated proof routes on MathlibMPR, covering up to 3.7% of extra groups. More importantly, we evaluate whether these retrieval gains translate into improved end-to-end theorem proving by integrating LeanGraphSearch into an iterative proving loop guided by Lean feedback. Across three theorem proving benchmarks, LeanGraphSearch improves pass rate at {8, 16, 32} reflection turns by as much as 40% compared to vanilla prover and at most 10% compared to LeanSearch v2, showing higher accuracy-cost efficiency. These findings highlight the value of dependency graph search for theorem proving and motivate further research on structure-aware search for proof discovery.

candidates.title: Deterministic, branch-selective optimization of peptidomimetic scaffolds reveals design principles for targeting TNF-α.
candidates.abstract: Tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) is a central driver of chronic inflammatory diseases, yet the development of non-biologic TNF-α inhibitors remains challenging due to the large, shallow nature of its protein-protein interface. Peptides offer a promising alternative to small molecules; however, rational optimization of complex peptide architectures such as branched or cyclic scaffolds remains a major bottleneck, as conventional approaches often rely on empirical screening or low-resolution mutagenesis. Here, we report a deterministic, branch-selective optimization strategy for a lysine-centered branched peptidomimetic TNF-α inhibitor using On-Demand Array Synthesis and Screening (ODAST). Through three iterative rounds of hypothesis-driven diversification, we systematically resolved the roles of charge identity, charge density, and cooperative aromatic interactions across distinct branches of the scaffold. This process led to the identification of a conserved bidentate anionic recognition motif, paired with aromatic and hydrogen-bonding elements that cooperatively stabilize TNF-α binding. The optimized peptides exhibited >10-fold improvements in apparent affinity and effectively inhibited TNF-α-induced cytotoxicity, with a lead compound displaying low-micromolar cellular IC

candidates.title: Multivalent Surface Search Dynamics Shape Bacteriophage Adsorption Efficiency: A Stochastic Model of Tail Fiber Optimization
candidates.abstract: Phages must locate and bind to bacterial surface receptors to initiate infection. Their tail fiber configuration critically influences this process. We develop a stochastic model describing surface search as a renewal process, incorporating attachment, detachment, and target-finding steps. Using both numerical simulations and analytical calculations, we quantify how tail fiber number, attachment-detachment rates, and geometric constraints impact the mean and the distribution of time to successful adsorption. Notably, the search efficiency shows a nonmonotonic dependence on tail fiber number, governed by a trade-off between binding stability and diffusion-mediated mobility. This optimum shifts depending on the effective bacterial density, target radius, and fiber reach. Short fiber reach imposes severe geometric constraints, reducing mobility at high tail fiber counts and leading to performance degradation. Our findings suggest that phage adsorption strategies are shaped by a balance between anchoring and exploration, with evolutionary implications for tail fiber design and infection efficiency.

candidates.title: Biologically inspired alignment reveals distributed and directionally asymmetric correspondence between rat and human cortices
candidates.abstract: Rodent models enable causal interrogation of brain circuits, but translating their systems-level organization to humans requires correspondence beyond one-to-one anatomical homology. Guided by the view that cortical areas are characterized by their relationships within distributed functional networks, we developed BrainMapping, a biologically inspired framework for aligning rat and human cortex using resting-state functional MRI. The framework combined a shared representation with optimal transport to derive probabilistic, bidirectional maps. These alignments revealed distributed, many-to-many correspondences that generalized to held-out subjects and preserved functional connectivity architecture, cortical gradients, and graph topology. Organizational preservation was directionally asymmetric. Human-to-rat mapping preserved organization more uniformly across rat cortical systems, whereas rat-to-human mapping showed stronger preservation in human association-related networks than in primary sensory and motor networks. The maps recovered literature-consistent default-mode and salience-system correspondences and generated testable non-canonical predictions. These findings provide a framework for expressing rat functional organization in human functional-network coordinates.

candidates.title: Grounding Generative Verification in 3D Content
candidates.abstract: Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and 3D generation have expanded 3D understanding and synthesis. However, beyond visual fidelity, task-specific correctness grounded in 3D evidence remains a major challenge. We argue that building reliable 3D systems requires not only stronger generation and reasoning, but also verification feedback that identifies unmet requirements and explains their violations, allowing systems to reflect on and refine their outputs. Such feedback must integrate multi-view observations and distinguish genuine inconsistencies from projection-dependent appearances. We make three contributions. First, we introduce 3DVerifierBench, a benchmark spanning 10 tasks that evaluates decisions, rejection explanations, and responses to controlled changes in specifications and candidates. A human study reveals a 21.6 percentage-point gap between humans and the strongest tested model, GPT-6 Astra, while explanation-aware analysis exposes weaknesses in rejection reliability. Second, we analyze verification across fine-grained factual categories, exposing errors in values and target binding. We develop a scalable pipeline combining multi-view fact extraction, controlled 3D editing, and native annotations to produce 14,126 training examples with contradiction explanations and linked counterfactuals. Third, we examine how verification could support 3D generation through candidate selection and recursive refinement. In human-labeled sixteen-candidate pools, oracle selection improves complete factual success from 26.7% to 90.0%. In a separate eight-input study, human-guided recursive refinement satisfies all seven requirements for every input, compared with three under parallel Oracle@8. Together, our benchmark, analysis, and data pipeline establish a foundation for models to reflect on 3D content through reliable verification feedback.

candidates.title: Metropolis-scale resilient and trustworthy traffic flow inference using multi-source data
candidates.abstract: Inferring network-wide traffic states from sparse observations with high accuracy and trustworthy uncertainty quantification is essential for intelligent transportation systems, yet it remains challenging due to the underdetermined nature of the problem, multifaceted disturbances in sensing networks, and the inherent conflicts among multiple inference subtasks when modeled jointly. We propose the Task-Aware Attentive Neural Process (TA-ANP), a unified probabilistic framework for resilient and trustworthy global traffic state inference (GTSI) by fusing floating car data (FCD) with sparse fixed-detector measurements. By casting GTSI as a stochastic process, TA-ANP leverages the meta-learning properties of neural processes to adapt rapidly to changes in sensing configurations without retraining. A task-aware multi-query attention module with distinct spatiotemporal inductive biases is introduced to jointly handle three GTSI subtasks—real-time estimation at unobserved locations, forecasting at both observed and unobserved locations—while mitigating cross-task interference. For uncertainty quantification, we combine neural processes with Monte Carlo Dropout to capture both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty. To support metropolis-scale evaluation, we construct the Metropolitan Multi-Source Traffic Dataset (MMTD), integrating fixed-loop sensor measurements, FCD statistics, and OpenStreetMap road-network data over an urban network of 26,166 road segments, including 2371 fixed-sensor-equipped segments used for quantitative evaluation. Experiments across multiple independently generated sensor configurations show that TA-ANP achieves best performance across all subtasks under deterministic and probabilistic metrics. The resulting well-calibrated uncertainties enable more efficient fixed-sensor placement with fewer sensor deployments. Under a Damage–Repair–Addition sensing lifecycle, TA-ANP demonstrates superior resilience in terms of disturbance absorption, performance recovery, and adaptability to unseen sensing configurations.The code and processed datasets are publicly available on GitHub and Zenodo , respectively.

candidates.title: Sequence-based artificial intelligence-guided inhibitory peptides to counteract AAV neutralizing antibodies in gene therapy.
candidates.abstract: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors have demonstrated strong clinical efficacy across multiple monogenic disorders, yet neutralizing antibodies (NAbs) remain major barriers to vector redosing and durable transduction. To address this limitation, we developed a sequence-based artificial intelligence framework integrating Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) and Evolutionary Scale Modeling with Low-Rank Adaptation (ESM-LoRA) to identify human-tolerant, virus-specific motifs across human and viral proteins using sliding-window analyses and multi-layer fine-tuning. Using capsid-derived segments from AAV2 and AAV843, we prioritized surface-accessible, virus-polarized peptides as candidate decoys and evaluated their ability to block AAV-targeted antibodies. The models achieved high accuracy in distinguishing human versus viral fragments, and selected peptides bound AAV-specific antibodies with nanomolar affinity, competitively restored capsid binding, and recovered >60% of baseline transduction in the presence of NAbs. In mouse models with pre-existing or redosing-induced antibodies, coadministration of decoy peptides and an IgG-degrading enzyme reduced high-titer NAbs to approximately 1:4 and restored hepatic transgene expression without detectable inflammatory or peptide-specific immune responses. A contrastive variational autoencoder (VAE) further generated non-natural peptides with broader epitope coverage. These results support sequence-driven AI design of short, low-immunogenicity decoy peptides as a translational strategy to mitigate NAb interference and enhance the feasibility of AAV redosing.

candidates.title: Fast Solution Methods for the Classical 0–1 Knapsack Problem
candidates.abstract: The classical 0--1 knapsack problem is among the simplest integer programs to state and among the most instructive problems for understanding why algorithm selection must follow instance structure. An input contains items with positive integer weights and profits, and the task is to choose a maximum-profit subset whose total weight does not exceed a capacity. The problem is weakly NP-hard, yet many large instances are solved quickly because exact algorithms exploit moderate numeric parameters, strong linear relaxations, dominance relations, or a small set of uncertain variables near the fractional break item. This review develops a theory-guided account of the principal fast solution methods for the classical problem. It proves the correctness and complexity of weight-indexed and profit-indexed dynamic programming, explains sparse Pareto-frontier implementations and reconstruction, derives the fractional-knapsack upper bound used by branch-and-bound methods, and establishes the correctness of meet-in-the-middle search. It then presents the core concept that underlies influential practical solvers and gives a detailed proof of the standard profit-scaling fully polynomial-time approximation scheme. Modern advances based on structured min-plus convolution are placed within this classical landscape rather than treated as isolated results. The central conclusion is that there is no universally fastest knapsack algorithm. Small item counts favor meet-in-the-middle search, moderate capacities or total profits favor dynamic programming, favorable density structure favors core-based exact methods, and very large numeric coefficients favor approximation. A final decision framework translates these theoretical distinctions into an implementable solver-selection policy while identifying open questions concerning adaptivity, certified switching among methods, memory efficiency, and realistic hard-instance generation.

candidates.title: Tipping point forecasting in nonstationary dynamics on function spaces
candidates.abstract: Tipping points are abrupt, drastic, and often irreversible changes in the evolution of nonstationary and chaotic dynamical systems. For instance, increased greenhouse gas concentrations are predicted to lead to drastic decreases in low cloud cover, referred to as a climatological tipping point. In this paper, we learn the evolution of such nonstationary dynamical systems using a recurrent neural operator (RNO), which learns mappings between function spaces. After training RNO on only the pre-tipping dynamics, we employ it to detect future tipping points using an uncertainty-based approach. In particular, we propose a conformal prediction framework to forecast tipping points by monitoring deviations from physics constraints (such as conserved quantities and partial differential equations), enabling forecasting of these abrupt changes along with a rigorous measure of uncertainty. We illustrate our proposed methodology on nonstationary ordinary and partial differential equations, such as the Lorenz-63 and Kuramoto–Sivashinsky equations. We also apply our methods to forecast a climate tipping point in stratocumulus cloud cover and airfoil wake and stall transitions using only limited knowledge of the governing equations. For the latter, we show that our proposed method zero-shot generalizes to forecasting multiple future tipping points under varying Reynolds numbers. In our experiments, we demonstrate that even partial or approximate physics constraints can be used to accurately forecast future tipping points.

candidates.title: Sequential Sampling as a Computational Principle of Episodic Memory
candidates.abstract: Visual perception unfolds through sequential eye movements, yet computational models of episodic memory typically assume that event representations already exist. Here, we propose that sequential gaze sampling does not simply supply memory with visual information, but contributes to the construction and organisation of episodic representations. We introduce a computational model in which successive fixations are integrated into an evolving internal representation, subsequently stored in associative memory and later retrieved through partial reinstatement of the original sampling trajectory. Within to-be-remembered elements, successive samples support progressive individuation; between elements, more frequent transitions strengthen relational binding. As sampling proceeds, internal representations become progressively lower-dimensional while retaining information about where samples were taken and when they occurred in the sequence. Sampling history also remains embedded in the resulting representation: changing the order of otherwise identical samples alters both the representation itself and element-specific retrieval. At retrieval, reinstating more of the original sampling trajectory improves access to specific elements, while competition is strongest when memories share both semantic category and sampling history. Finally, an exploratory generative readout shows that regions sampled during encoding are reconstructed more faithfully than unsampled regions. Together, these findings suggest that sequential sampling provides a candidate computational process through which episodic representations are constructed, shaping their subsequent storage and retrieval.

candidates.title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
candidates.abstract: Significant efforts are currently being directed toward the implementation of large-scale quantum information processors, but realizing useful quantum advantage also requires the development of efficient quantum algorithms. While for many practical problems the dominant resource costs are associated with a small set of computational primitives, optimizing them in the quantum setting presents unique challenges, including a reversibility constraint absent from ordinary classical computation. Here we introduce an evolutionary framework in which large language models (LLMs) propose circuit designs and an independent evaluator verifies and scores them. We apply this framework to tasks spanning numerical computation, chemistry, optimization, quantum simulation, and number theory. In seven of the eight tasks, the discovered circuits significantly reduce both Toffoli and qubit counts relative to the state of the art. In the eighth, the search discovers a new reversible architecture for prime-field modular inversion. By handling reversibility differently, the architecture makes divsteps -- a classical algorithm previously impractical for reversible integer arithmetic -- viable and substantially improves the Toffoli-qubit trade-off for modular inversion. These results open the door for evaluator-guided LLM co-design of new algorithmic structures for quantum computation.

candidates.title: A differentiable multi-physics learning model for robust single-image dehazing under complex atmospheric conditions
candidates.abstract: Restoring clear visibility from a single hazy image remains a challenging inverse problem when multiple atmospheric phenomena jointly affect image formation. In real environments, light propagation can be influenced not only by particle scattering but also by turbulence-induced blur and wavelength-dependent attenuation. Most existing dehazing approaches primarily address scattering, which limits their physical consistency and robustness in heavy haze or long-range scenes. In this work, we introduce a differentiable multi-physics learning framework that is designed to integrate scattering, turbulence, and spectral attenuation within a unified image formation model. The degradation process is expressed as a compact linear observation equation, where turbulence is represented through a spatial convolution operator and spectral effects are modeled via channel-dependent attenuation. Since the governing parameters cannot be directly inferred from a single observation, the formulated as an iterative refinement process guided by a learned approximation of the physical model. A lightweight neural estimator predicts the observation operators, while a learnable spectral module captures wavelength-dependent behavior. An iterative regularization network stabilizes the reconstruction process and prevents error propagation. Experiments conducted on the RESIDE-SOTS benchmark show competitive performance, achieving PSNR/SSIM values of 27.3/0.94 for indoor scenes and 30.2/0.94 for outdoor scenes with only a few optimization steps. Additional analyses confirm improved robustness under noise perturbations and severe illumination variations, highlighting the effectiveness of differentiable learning with physics-inspired constraints for real-world atmospheric image restoration.
